title: Choose the visual world below the hero
question: The roll assigned The Hallmark. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Hallmark
options.lineage: European assay offices and the hallmark strip: sponsor's mark · fineness · assay office · date letter · common control mark
options.thesis: A hallmark certifies that metal meets a legal fineness without saying which mine it came from. The page below the hero is a struck plate: every fact is punched into metal, and the row of five marks IS the product story (supplier mark sealed · share above the minimum · assayed by the circuit · lot and year · Compliant struck on chain). It refuses the SaaS scroll of cards and the cream editorial sheet alike.
materials: oxidised steel for the bench passage
options.viewport: Directly under the hero, one full-width plate carries five large struck marks in a row, each a cartouche in relief with its meaning set beneath in the slab; scroll strikes them one by one. Below it the plate continues as one uncut sheet through the law (size-only hierarchy), the assay (four states of one object with the hero's clips), the bench (dark passage with the three real screens), the register (public plate vs private book), the disclaimers, the questions and the assay certificate (the memo). Primary action stays the memo; the strike is the one authored motion.
options.risk: Precious-metal imagery can read as jewellery if the brass is allowed to shine; it must stay matte, industrial and measured, and the metaphor must never be explained in copy.

raised.raise: The legal section runs on size alone: article numbers at display scale, quotes beneath, one face, no cards, no eyebrows.
How it works is one object in four recoverable states, not four tiles; the same plate folds from supplier to verdict.
The four regulatory clocks are a strict ruled board with a cascading update and an amber lamp on the delayed act.
One continuous plate across the page with visible seams at section breaks, never stacked boxes.
Strike depth is a continuous state: marks deepen as the proof completes, one dimension of the display tied to state.
The verdict is announced before it lands: the console's bar fills, then the mark is struck.

options.label: The Test Report
options.lineage: TÜV / Intertek materials test reports: measured value, limit, PASS
options.thesis: The page as the notified body's own report on the car: every claim is a measured value against a limit line, specimen photos from the hero, PASS marks where the share clears the minimum.
options.viewport: A report header with model and regulation, then a results table at display scale: Recycled cobalt 17.2 % against a 16 % limit drawn as a line, the two pieces as specimens, the three screens as annexes.
options.risk: Also where most runs in this category land; familiar to the buyer, which is its strength and its ceiling.

options.label: Festival Lineup Sheet
options.lineage: one face, hierarchy by size and line breaks alone
options.thesis: The regulation and the product billed by importance: no imagery, size carries the whole argument.
materials: one condensed face at eight sizes
options.viewport: Article 52 spanning the width, Annex XIII and Art. 49(2) beneath, the limits packed at the foot.
options.case: Holds product clarity for the legal argument; loses identification, a compliance officer does not see themselves in a gig poster.
options.risk: Type-only pages need flawless setting or they read as a wall.

options.label: Orizuru Fold Sequence
options.lineage: one uncut sheet through numbered folds
options.thesis: The ledger as one sheet folded until only the verdict shows; every earlier crease still there, unread.
options.viewport: A single sheet in the first viewport that folds, step by step, from full bill of materials to a small standing verdict.
options.case: Strong product clarity: folding hides information without destroying it. Weak identification for a European compliance buyer.
options.risk: Reads as craft, not conformity assessment.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse Board
options.lineage: rail departure boards, rows ranked by time
options.thesis: The four regulatory deadlines and the eight lots as a ruled board that updates character by character.
options.viewport: A departures board of obligations: 18 Feb 2027 on top, the delayed act under an amber lamp, cascading flips on load.
options.case: Holds identification (European industrial signage) and is superb for the clocks; too narrow to carry the three screens and the ledger.
options.risk: One-trick when stretched across a whole page.

options.label: Itasha Vinyl Wrap
options.lineage: printed vinyl across car panels, sponsor strips along the sill
options.case: Sponsor strips for races that never happened are invented proof, and the culture is foreign to the buyer.
options.kept: One artwork across seams: the plate runs continuous across section breaks.

options.label: Chromatophore Skin
options.lineage: cephalopod skin as a living display
options.case: Neither identification nor clarity for conformity assessment.
options.kept: One display dimension tied to state: strike depth follows proof progress.

options.label: Algorave Source Floor
options.lineage: projected live code as the stage
options.case: Speaks to the developer first, which the brief forbids on this surface.
options.kept: Announce before it lands: the bar fills, then the mark is struck.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Deep-green SaaS scroll: product screenshots in rounded frames, three feature cards, logo wall, testimonial, FAQ, demo CTA, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Headline left, product screenshot right, partner logos beneath: the arrangement Minespider, Certifier and Vanta ship.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the six benchmarks by design, and it needs the logos and testimonials we do not have.
